neighbours.label: The last word of an abbreviated journal or publication name in a reference (Am Fam Physician, Dermatol Clin, journal Machine Learning)

Ng T. Night cough in adults. Am Fam Physician. 2009;79(2):110-4.
Okafor B. Statins and memory. Ann Intern Med. 2016;164(5):330-7.
Kim H, Ruiz P. Eczema treatment update. Dermatol Clin. 2020;38(1):55-63.
Weber S. Kernel methods revisited. Mach Learn. 2004;56(1):9-30.
Lund A. Anaemia in pregnancy. Obstet Gynecol Clin. 2011;38(2):201-9.

quiet: Doctors in the paediatric clinic saw many sports injuries in teens last year.
Her physician said the night cough would pass within a week.
The internal medicine ward added two beds for older patients.
The dermatology clinic opens early on Tuesdays for eczema patients.
Kernel methods are taught in most machine learning courses.
The midwife explained how anaemia is treated during pregnancy.
Office workers often complain of back pain after long days.
Her grandfather treated his gout with rest and cherries.

predictions: The final word of a journal title in a citation reaches 0.3-0.5; the same words (physician, clinic, medicine, learning) in ordinary prose stay under 0.06.
notes: Probe: 'Am Fam Physician' 0.368, 'Dermatol Clin' 0.358, 'the journal Machine Learning' 0.342, 'support.microsoft.com' 0.267; 'New England Journal of Medicine' in prose 0.041, 'family physician recommended' 0.031, 'Machine learning methods' 0.029.
